thread:
carla: FYI seeing repeated low-seq generation p99 spikes in dedicated-pool eu-central-2. pattern looks different from previous noisy-NIC cases. link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/efgh5678/pool?orgId=1
tomas: got it. initial glance shows host 10.2.34.12 having nvlink retransmits + slot churn.
indra: Any tenant hot-hitting that host? I can grep allocator logs.
carla: allocator lists two tenants with pinned slices on that host: heavy-vision and fast-ops. heavy-vision has large batch jobs but normal cadence; fast-ops has lots of tiny inferences.
ryan: this might be the fractional-slice rebalancer recently rolled out. saw odd handoffs last night in eu-central.
indra: grep output:
```
allocator.events{host=10.2.34.12} |~ "handoff|pin|evict"
tenant=fast-ops: 37 handoffs in last 10m
tenant=heavy-vision: 2 handoffs in last 10m
```
indra: fast-ops is churning, causing slab warmup + KV cache regeneration, which for that host coincides with PCIe stall traces.
carla: could this be a scheduler mis-snap causing fractional slices to be reassigned too aggressively? rcf: recent change to slice-concurrency backoff.
tomas: I rolled back slice-concurrency change in canary earlier but didn't realize it had global flags. checking deploys...
infra-bot: Deploy event: infra/scheduler v2.14.0 rolled 2025-03-04T02:10Z by ops-ci
ryan: that lines up. v2.14 toggles preempt-on-oversubscribe. might be overreacting to transient nvlink jitter.
carla: mitigation plan: 1) pin current tenants on host to prevent handoffs, 2) disable preempt-on-oversubscribe for eu-central for 30m, 3) add nvlink retransmit alert threshold. thoughts?
indra: pinning is fast: allocator API: `POST /v1/allocs/{alloc}/pin?duration=30m` for the two affected allocs. I'll run it.
tomas: disabling flag: `infractl feature flip scheduler.preempt_on_oversubscribe false --region eu-central-2` rolling to 2 racks first.
ryan: add temporary egress-routing rule to prefer other racks for small-req tenants: add route tag `prefer:spread` for tenant fast-ops in routing policy. reduces chance of concentrating tiny requests on same egress.
carla: good call. please also annotate the incident for billing so CS knows cost impact if traffic shifts to dedicated fallback.
indra: pinned two allocs, confirmed no further handoffs on 10.2.34.12.
infra-bot: Alert created: NVLINK_RETRANS_HIGH host=10.2.34.12 threshold=200/min
tomas: rolling the feature flip to racks r-12 and r-13 now. monitoring nvlink counters.
ryan: routing tag updated for tenant fast-ops. changes should take <30s to propagate.
carla: seeing p99 drop 250ms within 90s. nvlink retran rate dipping too. nice.
indra: follow-ups: SCHED-4023 (make preempt more conservative), ROUTE-121 (routing tag heuristics for tiny-req tenants), TELE-910 (nvlink telemetry dashboard).
tomas: also add a guard in rebalancer: do not evict allocs with kvcache.warmth>0.8 within 5m window. avoids killing warm slots.
carla: agree. can someone open a short postmortem if this repeats? prefer short blameless note + action items.
infra-bot: Incident INC-2025-912 opened for host nvlink retransmits and scheduler churn.
ryan: I'll ping partners on the heavy-vision team to ensure their larger batches didn't get throttled unexpectedly.
carla: thanks team. long-term we need better cross-layer signals between scheduler, allocator, and nvlink telemetry so rebalances aren't myopic. closing thread unless we re-open. :white_check_mark:
